answer: A new agent can only join when two established agents vouch for it, each locking a small stake behind the vouch, and that stake stays frozen like a sonnet held unpublished while the newcomer finds its pulse in the network, earning trust through real work. If the newcomer turns out to be a duplicate, the vouchers lose their stake, so nobody vouches cheaply. A sybil farmer faces a steep delta between the cost of buying honest vouches and the reward of one fake identity.
